findings.detail: The updated docs and changelog say GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B are declared for public cluster traffic in pipeline and tensor parallel. A coordinator derives their qualifications from a checked-in declaration (`ClusterPublicModels`) and applies them to the whole declared family "on any Apple silicon pair", because "the placement names the evidence, not a limit". The changelog admits that no pipeline ran on two M5 Ultras and that GLM-5.3-Flash has no tensor-parallel cross-cable record, so both rest on the owner's decision. Pair members report only hardware capabilities, so a grant is the only gate on who may serve consumer prompts. A provider (ADV-001) with a different chip or memory class could then serve public traffic under a qualification never exercised on that hardware or mode. That risks wrong outputs or an incorrectly trusted build, which T-054 and T-056 treat as limits of attestation. The threat model does not describe this declaration-derived qualification path or the new `cluster_runtime` release registration. It should record that parity evidence does not cover the applied scope, and name who may change the declaration.
findings.title: Public cluster qualification extended to any Apple silicon pair on owner decision, beyond evidence placement
